title: .NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates
author: Rahul Bhandari
note: .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and .NET 11 RC3 fix Brotli decompression and Linux tarball ownership issues, and complete fixes from the earlier October release. Update framework-dependent runtimes and restart apps; rebuild and republish self-contained apps and containers. RC2 users should move to RC3.

title: Microsoft.UI.Reactor: a C#-first way to build WinUI apps
author: Alexandre Zollinger Chohfi
note: An experimental framework that brings Model-View-Update to WinUI: interfaces are described in C# and native controls update as state changes. The walkthrough builds a counter as a .NET 10 file-based app. There is no support policy or API guarantee yet.

title: Memory-efficient JSON in .NET 10 web APIs with PipeReader
author: Ali Hamza Ansari
note: Compares stream-based JSON deserialization with the PipeReader support in System.Text.Json on a payload of one million readings, measuring time, allocations and garbage collections. Validate the results against your own workload.

title: Are Async Database Inserts Really Faster in .NET?
author: David McCarter
note: Benchmarks synchronous against asynchronous database inserts and challenges the assumption that async always finishes faster. A prompt to measure your own database workload. The full article needs a paid subscription.

title: Stop Blocking on the Database Inside IsValid: .NET 11 Validates Async
author: JKC
note: AsyncValidationAttribute, IAsyncValidatableObject and the async Validator APIs move database-backed checks out of blocking IsValid calls. Also covers cancellation, validation stages, the validateAllProperties flag and why synchronous validation paths need deliberate handling.

title: .NET tasks AI is better at than developers
author: David Grace
note: Uses Claude Code for project creation, unit tests, comments and exception debugging in an ASP.NET Core Web API. Reusable Markdown specifications define the architecture, packages, conventions and verification steps, giving the agent a clearer target.

title: Compare today’s code with an earlier commit
author: Leah Tran
note: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 adds Compare with Working Tree: pick a historical commit and see how your current files differ, uncommitted changes included, without switching branches. Every differing file is listed, not only those the commit touched.

title: Organize and revisit tabs with the keyboard
author: Mads Kristensen
note: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 adds Ctrl+Shift+PgUp/PgDn to move the active tab and Ctrl+NumPad1 to NumPad9 to jump to a visible tab in the active group. Pinned sections and project groups still apply; preview tabs cannot be moved.

title: Keep your investigation between sessions
author: Jason Chlus and Mads Kristensen
note: Create a standalone Markdown note through New File, and the opt-in Hot Exit preview in Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 restores unfinished notes and unsaved edits after reopening the IDE. Save the note when you want to share it or keep it in the repository.

title: JetBrains .NET Day Online 2026: Watch the Recordings
author: Mehul Harry
note: Recordings from the October 7 event: agent workflows in Rider, Outbox/Inbox/Saga messaging patterns, C# interceptors and Native AOT, and NuGet supply-chain attacks. The recap describes each session so you can pick a topic.

title: JetBrains GameDev Day 2026: Watch the Recordings
author: Anna Ruban
note: Sessions on Unreal Engine profiling, Unity UI automation, procedural generation in Godot, debugging across C# and C++, version control for game assets and evolving a live engine, grouped by engine and role.

title: C# Concepts Every .NET Backend Developer Should Know in 2026
author: qodors
note: A backend refresher on interfaces, asynchronous I/O and EF Core query optimization, with examples of the cost of blocking HTTP calls and loading more data than an endpoint needs.

title: This week in Cursor + .NET — 7 rules
author: Agentic Architect
note: Seven opinionated rules for reviewing agent-generated C#: value objects versus entities, sealed classes, strongly typed IDs, typed configuration, exception rethrowing, query tracking and DI lifetimes. Watch especially for singletons capturing scoped dependencies.

title: Azure DevOps Comes to Microsoft Copilot with Plugin for Work Items, Pull Requests
author: David Ramel
note: The Azure DevOps plugin for Microsoft Copilot reaches work items, pull requests, pipelines and test plans, and Cowork can turn requirements into structured backlogs. Check your organization has the required Copilot experience; Azure DevOps Server is not supported.

title: Announcing .NET 11 Release Candidate 2
author: .NET Team
note: RC2 is available with a go-live support license for production use. Highlights include incremental CBOR reading, configurable initial HTTP/2 concurrency, faster MSBuild wildcard matching and a CLI option for NuGet's minimum package publication age. Blazor's QuickGrid virtualization APIs are no longer experimental.

title: Introducing dotnetup: A toolchain manager for .NET
author: Chet Husk
note: A public-preview tool that installs and manages user-local SDKs and runtimes on macOS and Linux without administrator access. Stable, preview and daily builds can sit side by side, and dotnetup update refreshes tracked channels while leaving exact-version requirements pinned.

title: .NET and .NET Framework October 2026 servicing updates
author: Rahul Bhandari and Tara Overfield
note: Security and non-security fixes in .NET 10.0.13, 9.0.21 and 8.0.32. If you ship self-contained apps, update the bundled runtime and redeploy; check the versions your applications actually deploy, including container images.

title: Bring Your Own Model to the GitHub Copilot SDK with C#
author: Bruno Capuano
note: Keep the Copilot agent runtime while routing model requests to your own provider through ProviderConfig. The .NET 10 sample uses a Foundry or Azure OpenAI deployment with Microsoft Entra ID or an API key; pick a deployment that supports the Responses API.

title: Get Your .NET MAUI App Ready for Xcode 27
author: Gerald Versluis
note: Apps built with Xcode 27 need UIKit's scene lifecycle, and updating workloads alone won't change their platform files. For .NET 10 apps, use MAUI 10.0.110 or later and test authentication, deep links and App Actions too.

title: Durable Task in the Real World: What Problems Does It Actually Solve?
author: Tamir Dresher
note: Five examples cover approvals, Azure provisioning, subscription payments, out-of-order webhooks and an incident-response agent. Durable Task coordinates waits and recovery, but your application still owns authoritative state, idempotency and reconciliation.

title: Testing Payment Retries Without Charging Customers Twice
author: Vivek Kumar
note: Stable idempotency keys, explicit payment states and failure-focused testing in C#. The important case is a completed charge followed by a lost response: keep the outcome unknown until it can be reconciled, and verify the provider's own deduplication in its sandbox.

title: Why AI Agents Overstep and How to Build Agents That Stay Within Their Boundaries
author: Mahesh Chand
note: Tool permissions and application-side authorization, not instructions, decide what an agent can do. Check the user's identity, tenant, resource and requested operation before a tool runs, because an agent-generated approval flag isn't permission.

title: Stop waiting on a failed build
author: Mads Kristensen
note: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11 adds an opt-in setting to stop the solution build after its first project failure. Enable it when you usually fix the first error immediately; leave it off when you want diagnostics from the remaining projects.

title: A faster, lighter C# Dev Kit
author: Drew Noakes
note: Version 11.0 rebuilds the extension as one Native AOT process with cached project loading. In Microsoft's benchmark on the 407-project Aspire repo, full solution load drops from 84 s to 3 s and memory from about 2 GB to 316 MB; it's in pre-release for now.

title: Aspire 13.6: Your dashboard gets memory
author: Maddy Montaquila
note: The dashboard now keeps traces, logs and resource state after you stop the AppHost (up to 10 runs, stored locally in SQLite). You can go back to the run where a bug showed up, and the new opt-in WithRepl() opens a signed-in database shell right in the dashboard.

title: Microsoft is updating its NuGet author-signing certificate
author: NuGet Team
note: If you enforce trusted signers or run dotnet nuget verify with Microsoft fingerprints, installs fail with NU3034 until you add the new certificate fingerprint.

title: AG-UI Protocol now has a first-class .NET SDK
author: Daniel Roth
note: Microsoft and CopilotKit released an MIT-licensed .NET SDK for AG-UI, the open protocol for streaming agent events to user-facing apps. Any .NET service can now expose or consume agent endpoints that work with TypeScript and Python clients.

title: Build Agentic UI with the new Blazor AI components
author: Daniel Roth
note: The experimental Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.AI package renders streamed agent output, tool calls, approval prompts and shared state as Blazor components, on top of any IChatClient. Try it with the .NET 11 RC1 SDK and the AgenticUI sample.

title: Visual Studio September Update
author: Mark Downie
note: Bring Your Own Model (preview) now runs on the new Agent (Preview), with Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama. The old BYOM flow is gone and Ollama models need re-adding.

title: UWP and WinUI 3 apps: UI testing with MSTest
author: Amaury Levé
note: MSTest 4.5 can run UWP and WinUI 3 tests on the app's real UI dispatcher, across packaged, unpackaged and AppContainer hosts. Packaged hosts need Developer Mode, so check your CI agent first.

title: Experimental support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in ASP.NET Core
author: Andrew Lock
note: .NET 11 adds experimental DBSC support to ASP.NET Core with one call, AddDeviceBoundSession(...). It ties a login session to a key in the device's TPM, so a stolen auth cookie stops working quickly.

title: File-based apps can reference other C# files
author: Denis Makarenko
note: The new #:ref directive lets a dotnet run app.cs program pull in a second C# file. On .NET 11 RC1 it's still behind an experimental property.

title: What's Inside That Bearer Token? A Practical Guide to Encrypted JWTs (JWE) in .NET
author: Robert Dennyson
note: A walkthrough of spotting, inspecting and decrypting encrypted JWTs with JsonWebTokenHandler. Decryption and validation are separate steps, and any token pasted into a chat or log should be treated as exposed.

title: How to Make AI Write High-Quality Code in .NET
author: Anton Martyniuk
note: Rules written in prompts fade as an agent's context fills up, so the article moves them into the build with TreatWarningsAsErrors, analyzers, .editorconfig and Central Package Management.

title: Stripping extra dependencies in .NET NativeAOT apps using linker substitutions
author: Andrew Lock
note: An ILLink.Substitutions.xml file turns a runtime check into a constant, so the linker can remove code it couldn't prove was unused. In Andrew's case that cut a NativeAOT binary by 22 to 25 percent.
